evidence_note: Table 1 of a 2024 review lists National Hospital Abuja with 2 LINACs and 1 HDR brachytherapy unit, with no 'not operational' footnote. The hospital leadership said it has two linear accelerators: one funded by the federal government in 2017 and one donated by NNPC/SNEPCo in 2019. It said a maintenance agreement keeps downtime to three days or less. "We have two radiotherapy machines in the hospital."

NHA's first LINAC was taken out of service because the manufacturer stopped supplying spare parts. "In 2017, the original LINAC in Abuja was decommissioned because the manufacturer no longer provided spare parts."

An Elekta Synergy LINAC bought in 2014 sat for about three years because its shielded room (bunker) was not finished. "the LINAC was not installed and commissioned until the shielded bunker was completed in 2017."

NHA's two LINACs treat patients (the same paper puts capacity at 80 to 100 patients a day), but staff are not trained to use their advanced modes. "because of inadequate training, we are unable to perform those advanced radiation treatment techniques."

A survey of nine radiotherapy centres (data collected May 2020 to April 2021) recorded 3 radiation oncologists at NHA in its Table 2. "Radiation oncologist 2 — 2 3 3 3 9 3 3 28" (the NHA column is the 5th value).

Table 1 of a 2024 review lists UMTH with 2 LINACs and does not flag them as not operational. This was before the 2024 floods (see the flood row). "University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital (UMTH) NA 2 NA"

Hospital Clinical Oncology page. It is undated: the footer says (c) 2023 and the page says the department was commissioned on 8 March 2023. It lists two LINACs, two 'BRT' machines and a CT simulator. "including two {2} Linac, Two BRT machines, a modern CT simulator"

The same undated hospital page lists one permanent consultant clinical and radiation oncologist (the head of department), five visiting consultants, three registrars and a medical officer. "The Department has three registrars and a medical officer."
In March 2022 the CMD described a cancer centre costing over N5bn with 4 bunkers and 2 LINACs. Installation was still in progress at that date. "We have four bunkers with two linear accelerators"
Radiotherapy equipment at UMTH was destroyed by the 2024 floods. Patients were then referred to centres hundreds of kilometres away. "the hospital was left without functioning radiotherapy equipment"

A replacement LINAC worth N1.57bn was donated by a private individual. At handover it was not yet in use and still needed calibration and staff training. "expected to become operational within the coming weeks, following calibration and staff training"

An oncology centre was commissioned in July 2025 with a TrueBeam LINAC, a CT simulator and 3-D HDR brachytherapy. It was built and will be run by NSIA/MedServe as a public-private partnership, with two generators, transformers and solar power. Installed, not confirmed as treating patients. "Federal Teaching Hospital in Katsina is equipped with advanced technology including a" TrueBeam Linear Accelerator

A federal ministry release on the commissioning of the Katsina oncology centre. It names TrueBeam technology but gives no machine count, and NSIA and MedServe attended. "equipped with cutting-edge TrueBeam technology"
JUTH offered chemotherapy but had no radiotherapy machine, so patients travelled to Abuja. A July 2025 BusinessDay report lists JUTH among future NSIA oncology sites. "has no radiotherapy machine."

Report of the IARC 2025 assessment: 15 working machines in 8 states (Lagos, Enugu, Ebonyi, Cross River, Borno, Abuja, Kano, Sokoto), against a need of over 120. Power cuts and missing maintenance contracts are named as causes. No facility-level breakdown is given. "Nigeria has only 15 functional radiotherapy machines distributed across eight states"; "lack of maintenance contracts particularly in facilities outside the public-private partnerships framework"

A 2026 report citing a Nigerian Cancer Society assessment: about ten working machines nationally. Only 2 of 8 government-funded centres treat patients consistently, and the article blames erratic power, poor maintenance and no residency training for medical physicists. "Nigeria has barely ten functional radiotherapy machines for a population exceeding 200 million"

In February 2022 an ABUTH oncologist said NHA had the only working external-beam radiotherapy machine in all of northern Nigeria. "no single functional external beam radiotherapy machine in the whole of northern Nigeria" (with the National Hospital Abuja as the exception)
